criteria.note: Reran python3 scripts/selftest.py (53 passed, 0 failed), python3 .warp/validate.py all (exit 0), and ./scripts/verify.sh (GATE GREEN, exit 0). Then imported the REAL .warp/policy_check.py into a harness and pointed P.ROOT at temp dirs OUTSIDE the repo, restoring it after. valid_approval_for behaved exactly as AC1 requires across 13 independent checks: (a) an approval bound to a mid-range commit is accepted and the returned path is the temp approval file, not something else; (b) an approval bound to a commit NOT in the passed range returns None; (c) an in-range but expired approval returns None; (d) a non-canonical decision 'approve' in range returns None; (e) an approval with empty scope, empty-string scope.commit, or no scope key all return None (it does NOT match everything). Widening did not become accept-anything: an empty push range returns None, a missing expires_at returns None, and a real in-range commit binding is still required. The commit changed only valid_approval_for (param rename commit->commits, str coercion, range membership via startswith) and added push_range_commits; decision, expiry, and exact-commit prefix binding are all kept. Template twin plugin/templates/.warp/policy_check.py is byte-identical. The selftest's 4 new range-binding cases (accept in-range, reject out-of-range, reject expired, reject non-canonical) are hermetic, use an isolated temp proof root, and restore P.ROOT (lines 317/325/338).

The full push-time allow path (policy_check.py exit 0) is NOT demonstrable live at THIS commit, and I did not fake a green run. At f1f2991 policy_check.py main() exits 1 with 'No passing independent verdict bound to HEAD (f1f2991d8b81) or its parent'. That is correct behavior and the ONLY current blocker: WARP-0114's own verdict is this very file, not yet committed, so valid_verdict_for(HEAD) and valid_verdict_for(parent) are both None. I verified every other gate of the allow path independently. Read main(): the checks are ordered verdict -> protected-path approval -> emergency debt. valid_verdict_for is unchanged by this commit and still requires a pass/pass_with_notes verdict whose scope.commit prefixes the target commit with no blocking findings (confirmed: returns a path for 0de75f3, None for f1f2991). push_range_commits() live returns 9 commits (@{upstream}=origin/main..HEAD) with HEAD first and f1f2991 in the range; changed_files() uses the identical range spec strings and the identical HEAD~20..HEAD fallback, so the file audit and the approval check cannot disagree about what the push is. The real proof/WARP-0114/approval-dmitry.json binds to f1f2991 (in range, approved, unexpired to 2026-08-15) and valid_approval_for(real range) accepts an in-range approval. Negative demonstration reproduced at the mechanism level: with approvals removed (empty proof/ and copied-tree-minus-approvals) valid_approval_for returns None, so the protected-path block fires. Therefore, once a passing verdict bound to f1f2991 is committed (it lands in a later evidence commit whose parent is f1f2991, satisfying valid_verdict_for(parent) via the guard's parent-fallback), and the in-range approvals remain, main() reaches exit 0. Allow path is reachable by construction; each component observed green independently.

findings.text: Approval authorization is by commit-in-range only, not by the specific protected path or the specific commit that touched it. valid_approval_for never checks scope.paths (pre-existing), and after WARP-0114 any approved, unexpired approval bound to ANY commit in the push range satisfies the protected-path gate for ANY protected edit anywhere in that range. Observed live: valid_approval_for(real range) returned proof/WARP-0100/approval-dmitry.json (bound to 0de75f3, recorded to approve a scripts/verify.sh change), which now also authorizes WARP-0114's edit to .warp/policy_check.py because both commits sit in the same 9-commit push range. This is a genuine widening of the trust surface versus the old HEAD-exact binding, but it is exactly what AC1 sanctions ('ANY commit in the push range'), the old HEAD binding is unsatisfiable by construction, and path-scoped / self-separated approvals are explicitly out of scope (W9 of PLAN-0001). Fails closed in every degenerate case tested. Non-blocking; worth pinning path-scope binding in the W9 follow-up.

The spec's rollback line states 'nothing else in policy_check changes,' but the diff also made the approval glob deterministic (sorted(...) over proof/*/approval*.json) and reworded two block messages. Both are safe: sorted() makes which valid approval is returned deterministic (an improvement, not a weakening) and the message text is cosmetic. The substantive logic change is exactly the HEAD-to-range widening as claimed. The 'nothing else changes' phrasing slightly understates the diff; git revert of f1f2991 still restores cleanly as the rollback claims.

The selftest's 4 new range-binding cases cover accept-in-range, reject-out-of-range, reject-expired, and reject-non-canonical, but omit the 'no scope.commit must not match everything' guarantee. I verified that guarantee independently (empty scope, empty-string scope.commit, and missing scope key all return None), but adding it to scripts/selftest.py would close the gap between the enforced behavior and its regression coverage.

summary: Independent different-model review (opus, implementer was fable) of the HIGH-risk change to the protected enforcer .warp/policy_check.py at f1f2991. AC1 confirmed: reran selftest (53/0), validate all (exit 0), and verify.sh (GATE GREEN), then attacked valid_approval_for in an isolated out-of-repo proof root across 13 checks; it accepts an approved unexpired approval bound to any in-range commit and rejects out-of-range, expired, non-canonical-decision, and missing-scope approvals, and did not degrade into accept-anything (empty range and missing binding both reject). push_range_commits and changed_files share the identical range spec and HEAD~20..HEAD fallback, so audit and approval agree on the push. AC2 confirmed by construction, not by a faked green run: policy_check correctly exits 1 at f1f2991 solely because WARP-0114's own verdict (this file) is not yet committed; every other gate of the allow path was observed green independently (the real in-range approval is accepted, the verdict gate is unchanged and commit-bound, the negative demonstration blocks when approvals are removed), so the allow path is reachable once this verdict lands in the evidence commit whose parent is f1f2991. Three notes, zero blocking: the widening authorizes any in-range approval for any protected edit in the range (spec-sanctioned, path-scope deferred to W9), the rollback line understates two incidental changes (sorted glob, reworded messages), and the selftest omits the missing-scope case I verified by hand. Could not refute the spec claim; the previously unsatisfiable allow path is now reachable while decision, expiry, and exact-commit binding are all preserved.
